newsitem.title: UK: UK outlines five-year oil, gas exploration plan.
newsitem.headline: UK outlines five-year oil, gas exploration plan.

text.p: Britain's Labour government on Wednesday announced a five-year plan for offshore oil and gas exploration.
Outlining a timetable for licensing rounds over the lifetime of the new government, the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) set Britain's 18th offshore round for later this year.
The blueprint is designed to give oil companies the chance to sketch plans for both mature North Sea acreage and emerging frontier blocks.
"It will help oil companies to know what's coming up," said a DTI spokeswoman.
The department said the 18th round would cover mature areas in the north, central and southern North Sea and the Morecambe and Liverpool Bay areas of the Irish Sea.
A formal announcement will be made in the autumn giving 90 days notice for applications. Awards are scheduled for Easter 1998.
Each subsequent year licensing rounds would offer "a mixture of mature and semi-mature provinces," the DTI said.
A new frontier round, probably Britain's 21st, would be scheduled for the autumn of 2000, the department said.
The round would be timed to allow the re-offer of acreage relinquished in accordance with terms of licences awarded in previous frontier rounds.
The DTI also said agreement with the Faroe Islands on a maritime boundary would be swiftly followed by the issue of oil and gas exploration licences covering parts of the disputed area.
"Agreement in this disputed area will be followed as soon as practicable by the designation of the UK acreage for licensing and then by the early announcement of a round in that area," it said.

DTI officials were also working on a review of significant finds on the UK Continental Shelf which remain undeveloped or under-tested six years after discovery, with a view to encouraging companies to reconsider plans for them.
The department set October 3 as the deadline for applications to two out of round blocks west of Shetlands put on offer in March.
